question.text: Mohini Capital Cat II SSF (Special Situation Fund) wants to invest in Security Receipts (SRs) issued by an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC). Per Chapter 9, which restriction applies?

answer.text: No restrictions; any AIF can buy any ARC SR.
AIFs can buy SRs of ANY ARC without conflict-check.

AIFs CANNOT invest in SRs (a) issued by an ARC which is the AIF's portfolio investee company, or (b) where the SR becomes a related-party transaction (backed by underlying loans of the AIF's associate / group companies).
Only Cat III AIFs are permitted to invest in ARC SRs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'there are certain restrictions: (a) an AIF cannot invest in SRs issued by an ARC which is its portfolio investee company and (b) an AIF cannot invest in SRs that become related party transactions (backed by the underlying loans of its associate or group companies) due to potential conflict of interest.' The Trap: Options A and B ignore the conflict-of-interest carve-out. Option D inverts the rule — Cat II (not Cat III) is the specifically-listed QIB under SARFAESI for SR investments. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tested this in the all-cat Manager exam. XIX-A tests at distributor level. III-A/C (Compliance) covers the related-party-transaction framework. Manager's Pro-Tip: Run an automated conflict screen at deal entry: flag any ARC that (i) is in your portfolio or (ii) holds loans of your portfolio companies. The fund's compliance officer should sign off BEFORE the IC approves the SR bid — retrofit compliance attracts SEBI enforcement.
